name: Shoulder Instability / Recurrent Dislocation
definition: Symptomatic excessive translation of the humeral head relative to the glenoid, often following traumatic dislocation or due to multidirectional laxity.

investigations.principle: Acute radiographs confirm reduction and exclude fracture.
investigations.MRI: MRI/MR arthrogram evaluates labral/capsular injury when needed.
investigations.radiographs: Radiographs may show Hill-Sachs or glenoid bone loss.

amber: Recurrent traumatic instability, major bone loss or high-risk athletes may require surgical stabilization.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Amsa-sandhi/Snayu injury phenotype may be documented.

patientEducation.summary: Symptomatic excessive translation of the humeral head relative to the glenoid, often following traumatic dislocation or due to multidirectional laxity.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for severe/progressive neurological deficit, vascular compromise, infection/systemic illness, major trauma, sphincter change or other listed red flags.
